First listed 2025-06-09 · episode or wrap

Safe to Stay Invested? Decoding 2025 Stock Charts

Todd Sohn teaches trend, breadth, sentiment and relative-strength analysis, revises an earlier bear-market interpretation and remains constructive after the April rebound. His bullish market direction gained support, but proprietary backtests and most stock-level chart rankings lack reproducible tests. Eisman challenges false bottoms and draws attention to concentration and active-manager constraints. Long-duration caution, gold optimism and Bitcoin risk behavior are distinct views, not interchangeable diversification claims.

YouTube · 2025-06-09 ↗Substack · 2025-06-09 ↗
Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

How he reasons here

  • Chart patterns are conditional clues rather than substitutes for fundamentals.
  • Look through headline indices and fund names to constituent breadth and overlapping exposures.
  • Separate price direction from inferred investor motives.
  • A risk-management threshold is not an unconditional price forecast.

Tools and charts discussed

Mentioned in the transcript; visual charts have not all been inspected.

  • 50-/200-day moving averages
  • One-month new-high breadth and 3/6/12-month backtests
  • Cap-weight versus equal-weight indices
  • Discretionary/staples and high-/low-beta ratios
  • ETF flow dashboard, VIX, put/call ratios and leveraged long/short AUM
  • Long-duration returns after first Fed cuts
